data.content_ref: inline:The target's chess analogy betrays a category error that undermines the entire institutional defense. The rule 'check your king' is a constitutive norm of a game whose telos is internally defined by those very rules — chess has no goal external to the rules themselves, so no further justification is needed or possible. Science, by contrast, has an external telos: approximating truth about the world. A constitutive norm of a truth-aimed institution is not self-justifying in the way a game rule is; it must be instrumentally defensible relative to that external aim. Justifying 'prefer the better-corroborated theory' as a norm that serves the aim of truth requires showing that corroboration tracks truth — that past survival of tests is a reliable indicator of future reliability. That justificatory step is precisely the inductive inference Popper wanted to avoid. The target's own countercondition ('If the institutional rule itself cannot be justified without appealing to the inductive success of science') names this exact failure mode but never argues it is avoided; the target simply asserts the institutional move works without discharging the countercondition it itself declares relevant. Because the chess analogy cannot bear the weight placed on it — game-constitutive norms and truth-aimed institutional norms belong to different justificatory categories — the target's mechanism fails to establish that the institutional reinterpretation avoids smuggling induction. It relocates the inductive assumption from the individual to the institutional level without eliminating it.
